In the school counsellor's room, Suraj, fifteen, slouched in the chair. Shalini, the counsellor, had called him in after his class teacher said he'd been snapping at everyone.
"How's this term?" Shalini asked.
"Fine."
"I noticed you've been sitting with different groups."
Suraj shrugged. "In June it was the cricket guys. Then the gamers. Now the ones who do music." He picked at his sleeve. "I don't know. I keep trying to be someone and it doesn't fit."
"And that feels…?"
"Weird. Annoying. Like I'm wearing someone else's clothes all the time. Then I get angry at everyone."
Shalini nodded. "It's really unsettling. And it's also very normal at your age. You're trying things on to find what fits."
Suraj looked up. "So I'm not messed up?"
"No. You're building a self. It's messy."

qa.a: The cricket guys.
